brief.meaningEn: Reduce someone’s worry, pressure or responsibility.
brief.meaningZh: 減輕某人的擔心、壓力或責任負擔。
brief.grammar: Take a/the/some weight, a lot of that weight, or a lot of pressure off someone’s shoulders; took/taken and lifted that weight are also possible. The context should establish the burden, whose shoulders it is lifted from, and what responsibility remains.
brief.register: Conventional burden-relief metaphor; a colleague may use weight for shared work, while a household member may use pressure for financial reassurance. Relief may be partial.
brief.boundaryZh: 減輕可以是部分或暫時，不表示一切責任消失；本課不是卸下實際背包。
brief.misconceptionZh: 要說明原來負擔及甚麼帶來舒緩，不能單靠休息就聲稱實際工作已完成。
brief.outcomeZh: 能把具體支援連到負擔減輕，同時保留未完成責任。

options.en: Part of the organiser’s burden was reduced while some work remained.
options.zh: 主辦者的部分負擔減輕，但仍有工作。

options.en: The organiser handed over the final schedule as well as all the calls.
options.zh: 主辦者把最後時間表及所有電話也交出。

options.en: The other organiser only offered sympathy and did not share any calls.
options.zh: 另一位主辦者只表示同情，沒有分擔電話。

options.en: The organiser received more calls to manage alone.
options.zh: 主辦者收到更多要獨自處理的電話。

listening.explanationZh: 分擔電話是具體支援，但時間表仍要準備，並非把責任全數轉交。
listening.en: Sharing the calls with another organiser took the weight off my shoulders, though I still had to prepare the final schedule.
listening.zh: 與另一位主辦者分擔電話聯絡，減輕了我的負擔，但我仍要準備最後時間表。

reply.promptEn: How did the other organiser’s help affect your workload?
reply.promptZh: 另一位主辦者的協助，怎樣影響你的工作負擔？

options.en: I could focus on the schedule because the calls were shared.
options.zh: 電話有人分擔，我可專注時間表。

options.en: It took a weight off my shoulders during the preparations.
options.zh: 準備期間，它減輕了我的負擔。

options.en: I had fewer people to contact on my own.
options.zh: 我需要獨自聯絡的人少了。

options.en: The support made the remaining work feel more manageable.
options.zh: 這份支援令餘下工作感覺較可應付。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都說明分擔後的好處；金句不用聲稱所有工作完成。

scene.promptZh: 朋友幫你核對報名表，你不再獨自擔心漏資料，但仍需寄確認信。哪句貼切？

options.en: Her help took a weight off my shoulders, though I still need to send the confirmations.
options.zh: 她的協助減輕了我的負擔，但我仍需寄確認信。

options.en: She has taken over sending the confirmations, and I have no remaining role.
options.zh: 她已接手寄確認信，我沒有餘下角色。

options.en: I now need to check every form alone without any support.
options.zh: 我現在要沒有支援地獨自核對每張表。

scene.explanationZh: 核對有人幫而確認信仍待寄，支持部分負擔減輕。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不足以說明有人 took a weight off your shoulders？

options.en: They shared a task that had been worrying you.
options.zh: 他們分擔令你擔心的工作。

options.en: They added another urgent task while leaving all existing responsibilities with you.
options.zh: 他們加一項緊急工作，原有責任仍全留給你。

options.en: Their clear answer reduced uncertainty about an important decision.
options.zh: 他們清楚回答，減少重要決定的不確定。

contrast.explanationZh: 加工作且沒有減少原負擔，不支持舒緩；分擔或減少不確定才有連繫。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴想幫你減輕活動壓力，但未確認便代你承諾更多工作。哪句回應最好？

options.en: Sharing the registration checks would take a weight off my shoulders; please agree any new commitments with me first.
options.zh: 分擔核對報名會減輕我的負擔；新增承諾前，請先與我議定。

options.en: Add the new tasks to my list first and leave the registration checks unchanged.
options.zh: 先把新工作加到我的清單，核對報名仍照舊。

options.en: Tell the group I have more capacity before asking which work I need help with.
options.zh: 未問我需要哪項協助，先告訴小組我可做更多。

dialogue.explanationZh: 具體分擔回應負擔，新增承諾前先確認，避免幫忙反增壓力。

speaking.en: Sharing the checks would take a weight off my shoulders, even though I would still manage the final list.
speaking.zh: 分擔核對會減輕我的負擔，但最後名單仍由我管理。
speaking.promptZh: 你想清楚提出所需支援及保留責任。先聽，再說。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你因要獨自安排社區餐會而擔心，鄰居答應處理購物，你仍負責出席名單。用一至兩句英文說明協助帶來的改變。

examples.en: My neighbour’s offer to handle the shopping took a weight off my shoulders. I could focus on the attendance list instead.
examples.zh: 鄰居提出處理購物，減輕了我的負擔。我可以改為專注出席名單。

examples.en: Having someone else organise the shopping took a heavy weight off my shoulders, although I still had to manage the attendance list.
examples.zh: 有人處理購物，令我的沉重負擔減輕，但我仍要管理出席名單。

writing.selfCheckZh: 連結購物分擔與負擔減輕，保留自己管理名單；不要寫成所有責任轉交。

takeaways.en: After a week of last-minute route changes, the agreed backup plan took a lot of that weight off the volunteers’ shoulders.
takeaways.zh: 一星期不斷臨時改路線後，議定的後備計劃大大減輕義工肩上的負擔。

takeaways.en: Knowing the rent was covered for another month took a lot of pressure off her shoulders, although she still needed to plan ahead.
takeaways.zh: 知道下個月租金已有着落，大大減輕她的壓力，儘管她仍須作長遠安排。

brief.meaningEn: A feeling that one’s actions have meaning or a worthwhile direction.
brief.meaningZh: 覺得自己的行動有意義，或有值得投入的方向。
brief.grammar: give someone a sense of purpose; find/gain a sense of purpose through an activity.
brief.register: Natural reflective collocation; a personally meaningful aim need not be a grand public achievement.
brief.boundaryZh: 有方向感不等於每天愉快、目標已完成或只可能來自有薪工作。
brief.misconceptionZh: 應指出行動為何重要，不能只按地位或外界認可判斷別人的意義。
brief.outcomeZh: 能把個人投入連到覺得有意義的原因。

listening.promptZh: 這項工作對說話者有甚麼意義？

options.en: It gave them a worthwhile direction through seeing the help it offered.
options.zh: 看見工作提供協助，令他們有值得投入的方向。

options.en: It was valuable only because it brought a higher job title.
options.zh: 它有價值，只因帶來較高職銜。

options.en: They had already completed all the learners’ long-term goals.
options.zh: 他們已完成所有學習者的長遠目標。

options.en: They joined without knowing whether the sessions helped anyone.
options.zh: 他們參加時不知道課堂是否幫到任何人。

listening.explanationZh: because 連到日常自主的實際好處，是行動有意義的線索，不是職銜或目標全完成。
listening.en: Helping adults practise reading gave me a sense of purpose because I could see how the sessions supported their everyday independence.
listening.zh: 幫成人練習閱讀，令我覺得所做的事有意義，因為我看見課堂如何支援他們日常自主生活。

reply.promptEn: Why do you continue volunteering at the reading sessions?
reply.promptZh: 你為甚麼繼續在閱讀課堂當義工？

options.en: I can see how the practice helps people manage daily tasks.
options.zh: 我看見練習如何幫人處理日常工作。

options.en: The work gives me a sense of purpose.
options.zh: 這份工作令我覺得所做的事有意義。

options.en: Supporting the learners is something I find worthwhile.
options.zh: 支援學習者，是我覺得值得做的事情。

options.en: I value being able to contribute to their independence.
options.zh: 能為他們的自主生活作貢獻，我很珍惜。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都解釋投入原因；金句說主觀的有意義方向，不以薪金或職銜作唯一標準。

scene.promptZh: 一位學生定期整理社區食物分享站，看見人們得到所需用品，覺得這份投入值得。哪句合適？

options.en: The work gives her a sense of purpose.
options.zh: 這份工作令她覺得所做的事有意義。

options.en: She values the work only as a title to add to her profile.
options.zh: 她只把工作視為可加到個人介紹的名銜。

options.en: She feels the activity has no connection with anything she cares about.
options.zh: 她覺得活動與她關心的事情沒有關係。

scene.explanationZh: 看見幫助及覺得值得，支持意義感，而非純名銜或毫無關聯。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個推論不宜由 a sense of purpose 得出？

options.en: A person feels their activity has meaning.
options.zh: 有人覺得自己的活動有意義。

options.en: Their work must be enjoyable and easy at every moment.
options.zh: 他們的工作必定每刻都愉快容易。

options.en: The feeling may come from a modest but valued contribution.
options.zh: 這份感覺可來自不大卻受珍惜的貢獻。

contrast.explanationZh: 有意義的工作仍可能辛苦或平凡，不能把方向感等同每刻輕鬆。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說整理分享站很平凡，不可能帶來人生意義，問你怎樣看。哪句最好？

options.en: It can give someone a sense of purpose if the contribution matters to them; ask what they value about helping.
options.zh: 若這份貢獻對某人重要，它可帶來意義感；問問對方珍惜協助的哪方面。

options.en: Judge its meaning only by how impressive the job title sounds.
options.zh: 只按職銜聽來多出色，判斷它的意義。

options.en: Remove the ordinary tasks from the account and describe only public recognition.
options.zh: 從描述刪掉平常工作，只寫公開認可。

dialogue.explanationZh: 意義可來自實際貢獻及個人重視，不必是響亮職銜或公開表揚。

speaking.en: Helping with a useful task gives me a sense of purpose, even when the work is ordinary.
speaking.zh: 即使工作平凡，幫忙做有用的事也令我有意義感。
speaking.promptZh: 你想說清平凡貢獻為何值得。先聽，再說。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你整理祖父母的舊相片及文字紀錄，了解家族故事，想製成相簿與家人分享，覺得這項個人計劃值得持續投入。用一至兩句英文解釋意義。

examples.en: Restoring our family archive gives me a sense of purpose. I want to connect the photographs with the stories behind them.
examples.zh: 整理修復家族資料，令我有意義感。我想把相片與背後故事連起來。

examples.en: Learning about our family history gives me a sense of purpose as I organise the photographs and records into an album to share with my family.
examples.zh: 我把相片及紀錄整理成相簿，與家人分享；了解家族歷史，令我有意義感。

writing.selfCheckZh: 把意義連到家族歷史、相片故事及分享計劃，不只籠統說忙碌，也不把有薪工作當唯一來源。

takeaways.en: Volunteering gave him a sense of purpose beyond his usual routine.
takeaways.zh: 義工工作令他在平常規律以外，有所做事情有意義的感覺。

takeaways.en: A sense of purpose can come from a small contribution that matters to someone.
takeaways.zh: 意義感可來自一份對某人重要的小貢獻。

sources.sentence: Without guidance, the team felt it was treading water.

brief.meaningEn: Make effort without getting closer to the desired outcome.
brief.meaningZh: 付出努力，卻沒有更接近想要的結果。
brief.grammar: be treading water; feel as if one is treading water; explain the stalled goal.
brief.register: Conventional swimming metaphor, distinct from actually staying afloat in a pool.
brief.boundaryZh: 不是完全沒有工作，也不表示永遠無法改善；常須改方法、方向或支援。
brief.misconceptionZh: 忙碌不一定有進展；也不能只憑進度慢就斷言毫無所得。
brief.outcomeZh: 能以重複活動與未接近目標的線索，描述停滯。

listening.promptZh: 團隊為甚麼這樣形容工作？

options.en: They were busy but not moving closer to answering the central question.
options.zh: 他們很忙，卻沒有更接近回答核心問題。

options.en: They had stopped working on the outline altogether.
options.zh: 他們已完全停止修改大綱。

options.en: They had finished the main question and were polishing the final answer.
options.zh: 他們已完成主要問題，只在潤飾最後答案。

options.en: Each rewrite had resolved a different major issue.
options.zh: 每次重寫都解決不同主要問題。

listening.explanationZh: 重寫不等於沒工作；但核心未解支持未接近目標，而非已完成或每次解決問題。
listening.en: We kept rewriting the same outline without resolving the main question, so the team felt it was treading water.
listening.zh: 我們不停重寫同一大綱，卻沒有解決主要問題，所以團隊覺得努力卻沒有進展。

reply.promptEn: Why do you want feedback before rewriting the outline again?
reply.promptZh: 再次重寫大綱前，你為甚麼想要回饋？

options.en: The last few rewrites did not help us answer the main question.
options.zh: 之前幾次重寫沒有幫我們回答主要問題。

options.en: We seem to be treading water with the same unresolved issue.
options.zh: 同一問題未解，我們似乎一直努力卻沒有進展。

options.en: We need to know which part of the approach is holding up progress.
options.zh: 我們要知道方法哪部分阻礙進度。

options.en: Another revision may repeat the same weakness unless we clarify the aim.
options.zh: 若不釐清目標，再改可能重複同一弱點。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都解釋先求回饋的理由；金句不是說沒有付出，而是未有實質進展。

scene.promptZh: 小組每天開會卻一再重談同一問題，沒有作決定，也未更接近可行方案。哪句合適？

options.en: The group is treading water and needs a clearer decision process.
options.zh: 小組一直努力卻沒有進展，需要更清楚決策程序。

options.en: The group has already agreed a workable solution and is implementing it.
options.zh: 小組已議定可行方案，正在實行。

options.en: The group has not met or discussed the problem at all.
options.zh: 小組從沒開會，也沒討論問題。

scene.explanationZh: 反覆有活動卻未接近方案，才支持停滯；不是已實行或從沒投入。

contrast.promptZh: 哪句是實際游泳動作，不是本課的進展比喻？

options.en: We are treading water because repeated meetings have not clarified the goal.
options.zh: 反覆開會仍未釐清目標，我們一直努力卻沒有進展。

options.en: The swimmer was treading water near the pool wall while waiting for the instructor.
options.zh: 泳者在池邊踩水，等導師。

options.en: The project felt as if it was treading water without a decision.
options.zh: 未有決定，項目感覺一直努力卻沒有進展。

contrast.explanationZh: 泳池及泳者是實際動作；項目或會議才是付出卻停滯的比喻。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴說每晚都重做大綱，既然很忙就毋須改方法，但核心仍未清。哪句建議最好？

options.en: If we are treading water, let us clarify the main question and get feedback before another rewrite.
options.zh: 如果我們一直努力卻沒有進展，再重寫前先釐清主要問題，並取得回饋。

options.en: Count the hours spent rewriting and use that as the only measure of progress.
options.zh: 數重寫用了多少小時，把它作為進展的唯一尺度。

options.en: Polish the headings again before checking whether the outline answers the question.
options.zh: 未查大綱有沒有回答問題，就再次潤飾標題。

dialogue.explanationZh: 要處理未接近核心的原因；時數及表面修飾不能代替方向檢查。

speaking.en: We may be treading water, so let us check whether our work is getting us closer to the goal.
speaking.zh: 我們可能一直努力卻沒有進展，所以先查工作有沒有令我們更接近目標。
speaking.promptZh: 你想指出停滯，也提出檢查方向。先聽，再說。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你的目標是用新詞組句，每天抄生字表，卻仍不會在句中使用。你想先請老師建議有效練習方法。用一至兩句英文指出停滯及下一步。

examples.en: I feel I am treading water by copying word lists without using the words. I want advice on practising simple sentences.
examples.zh: 一直抄生字表卻沒有使用詞語，我覺得自己努力卻沒有進展。我想請教怎樣練習簡單句子。

examples.en: I have been treading water with my vocabulary practice, so I will ask my teacher how to use the words in sentences.
examples.zh: 詞彙練習一直努力卻停滯，所以我會問老師怎樣在句中使用詞語。

writing.selfCheckZh: 把停滯限定於用新詞組句這個目標，保留已有付出，提出改練習方法；不要說抄寫在任何情況都沒有用。

takeaways.en: Without a clear aim, the team felt it was treading water.
takeaways.zh: 沒有清楚目標，團隊覺得一直努力卻沒有進展。

takeaways.en: We stopped treading water when feedback helped us resolve the main issue.
takeaways.zh: 回饋幫我們解決主要問題後，我們不再努力卻停滯不前。

sources.sentence: Good news put a spring in my step.

brief.meaningEn: Noticeable energy or cheerfulness, often reflected in the way someone walks.
brief.meaningZh: 明顯的活力或愉快，常反映在步伐上。
brief.grammar: put a spring in someone’s step; walk/leave with a spring in one’s step.
brief.register: Conventional movement image; often follows welcome news or a positive experience.
brief.boundaryZh: 不是步伐的精確速度，也不是春天季節；興奮仍不代表其他問題已解決。
brief.misconceptionZh: 要有振奮、活力或好消息線索，不能單憑跑得快就推斷心情。
brief.outcomeZh: 能把正面經歷與顯得較有活力的狀態連起來。

listening.promptZh: 說話者怎樣描述她的狀態？

options.en: She seemed cheerful and energetic after the invitation.
options.zh: 獲邀後，她顯得愉快而有活力。

options.en: She was rushing only because she was late for a train.
options.zh: 她只是因趕火車遲到而急走。

options.en: She had lost interest in attending the next rehearsal.
options.zh: 她已不再想參加下次排練。

options.en: She had been given a precise instruction about how fast to walk.
options.zh: 她收到步行速度的精確指示。

listening.explanationZh: 微笑及期待練習支持振奮；不是趕車、失去興趣或量速度。
listening.en: Being invited to perform put a spring in her step; she left rehearsal smiling and looking forward to the next session.
listening.zh: 獲邀演出令她心情振奮、步履輕快；她笑着離開排練，期待下次練習。

reply.promptEn: How did the invitation affect her after rehearsal?
reply.promptZh: 排練後，那份邀請對她有甚麼影響？

options.en: She left smiling and excited about the next session.
options.zh: 她笑着離開，對下次練習感到興奮。

options.en: It put a spring in her step.
options.zh: 它令她心情振奮、步履輕快。

options.en: She seemed more energised by having a performance to work towards.
options.zh: 有演出可努力準備，令她顯得更有活力。

options.en: The news gave her something positive to look forward to.
options.zh: 消息讓她有正面的期待。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都可自然描述邀請後的振奮；金句不是實際安裝彈簧。

scene.promptZh: 學生收到作品入選通知，微笑着走出課室，也興奮談下一個項目。哪句合適？

options.en: The good news put a spring in her step.
options.zh: 好消息令她心情振奮、步履輕快。

options.en: She left looking discouraged and unwilling to discuss future work.
options.zh: 她離開時顯得灰心，不願討論未來作品。

options.en: She was only walking quickly to avoid being late, with no change in mood described.
options.zh: 她只是為免遲到而快走，沒有描述心情改變。

scene.explanationZh: 微笑及興奮談項目，才支持活力及愉快，不是只有步速。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不足以支持 a spring in his step 這種心情描述？

options.en: He smiles and looks energised after welcome news.
options.zh: 收到好消息後，他微笑且顯得有活力。

options.en: He walks fast only to catch a bus, with no evidence about how he feels.
options.zh: 他只為趕巴士快走，沒有感受方面的線索。

options.en: He leaves the meeting cheerful and eager to begin the new project.
options.zh: 他愉快地離開會議，急不及待開始新項目。

contrast.explanationZh: 快走可以有其他原因；需要活力、愉快或正面期待等線索。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴見有人趕巴士走得快，就想用這個片語形容他很開心。哪句提醒最好？

options.en: A spring in his step suggests energy or cheerfulness; check the context rather than infer his mood from speed alone.
options.zh: 心情振奮、步履輕快表示活力或愉快；要看情境，不只憑速度推斷心情。

options.en: Use the walking speed as the complete evidence and leave out whether he was rushing.
options.zh: 把步速當全部證據，略去他是否趕時間。

options.en: Explain the idiom using only walking speed and leave out its meaning of energy or cheerfulness.
options.zh: 只用步速解釋片語，略去活力或愉快的意思。

dialogue.explanationZh: 趕車是快走的其他原因；本課要看心情及活力線索。

speaking.en: The invitation put a spring in my step and gave me something to look forward to.
speaking.zh: 邀請令我心情振奮、步履輕快，也讓我有了期待。
speaking.promptZh: 你想把好消息與振奮狀態連起來。先聽，再說。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：多年沒見的好友終於確認回來相聚，你收到訊息後，開心地離開工作場所走回家，期待見面。用一至兩句英文描述振奮反應。

examples.en: The news of our reunion put a spring in my step. I walked home feeling cheerful and looking forward to seeing my friend.
examples.zh: 重聚消息令我心情振奮、步履輕快。我愉快地走回家，期待見到朋友。

examples.en: I left work with a spring in my step after my old friend confirmed the visit; we would finally have time to catch up.
examples.zh: 老朋友確認到訪後，我心情振奮、步履輕快地離開工作場所；我們終於有時間敘舊。

writing.selfCheckZh: 交代確認重聚這件喜事，及輕快步伐、期待相見的感受；比喻不是實際彈簧，也不表示所有煩惱消失。

takeaways.en: The encouraging reply put a spring in my step.
takeaways.zh: 鼓勵的回覆令我心情振奮、步履輕快。

takeaways.en: She left with a spring in her step after hearing the good news.
takeaways.zh: 聽到好消息後，她心情振奮、步履輕快地離開。

sources.sentence: Small wins helped the trainees continue.

brief.meaningEn: Modest successful steps that can support confidence or motivation during a larger task.
brief.meaningZh: 在較大任務中，可支持信心或動力的小幅成功。
brief.grammar: small wins; a small win; celebrate/notice/build on small wins.
brief.register: Natural coaching and reflective collocation; wins need not be victories over another person.
brief.boundaryZh: 是實際的小進展，不等於整個目標完成，也不是把沒做的事當成果。
brief.misconceptionZh: 應有可指出的成功步驟，肯定進展後仍須面對未學會部分。
brief.outcomeZh: 能辨認可驗證的小成果，並把它連到繼續練習。

listening.promptZh: 這項成果在學習中有甚麼位置？

options.en: It was a completed step within a wider set of skills still to learn.
options.zh: 它是已完成的一步，仍有更多技巧要學。

options.en: It meant the trainees had mastered every kind of bicycle repair.
options.zh: 它表示學員已掌握所有單車維修。

options.en: It was only an intention to try, with no skill practised yet.
options.zh: 它只是打算嘗試，還沒練到技巧。

options.en: It depended on defeating the other trainees in a competition.
options.zh: 它取決於在比賽擊敗其他學員。

listening.explanationZh: 學會換胎是具體一步，before more difficult repairs 保留後續學習；不是全掌握或一定比賽。
listening.en: Learning to replace a bicycle tyre gave the trainees a small win before they moved on to more difficult repairs.
listening.zh: 學會更換單車輪胎，讓學員在進入更難維修前，先有一項小成果。

reply.promptEn: What helped the trainees feel ready to keep learning?
reply.promptZh: 甚麼幫學員覺得可以繼續學？

options.en: They could point to one repair they had learnt to complete.
options.zh: 他們能指出一項已學會完成的維修。

options.en: Small wins helped them see that their practice was making a difference.
options.zh: 小成果讓他們看見練習帶來分別。

options.en: Completing a manageable task gave them confidence for the next stage.
options.zh: 完成可應付的工作，給他們進入下一階段的信心。

options.en: They had evidence of progress rather than only a distant final goal.
options.zh: 他們有進展證據，不只有遙遠的最終目標。

reply.explanationZh: 四句均解釋繼續的動力；金句要有實際完成的小步驟。

scene.promptZh: 初學者終於能自行縫好一道直線，雖然還不會完成整件衣服，卻願意繼續練。哪句合適？

options.en: That small win gave her a reason to keep practising.
options.zh: 那項小成果給她繼續練習的理由。

options.en: She has already completed the whole clothing project independently.
options.zh: 她已獨自完成整個製衣項目。

options.en: She has not tried the skill and is only planning her first attempt.
options.zh: 她還沒試過技巧，只在計劃首次嘗試。

scene.explanationZh: 能獨自縫直線是已取得的成果，仍不會全件衣服就不等於完成全部目標。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜只憑 small wins 得出？

options.en: There have been modest successful steps.
options.zh: 已有小幅成功的步驟。

options.en: The entire long-term goal is necessarily finished.
options.zh: 整個長遠目標必然已完成。

options.en: The successes may encourage further effort.
options.zh: 這些成功可能鼓勵進一步投入。

contrast.explanationZh: 小成果可支持動力，但仍是部分，不是完成全部目標。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友只完成一道練習就想寫「已掌握整個單元」，問怎樣改得更準確。哪句最好？

options.en: Call it a small win and say which skill improved, then identify what you will practise next.
options.zh: 稱它為小成果，交代哪項技巧進步，再指出接下來練甚麼。

options.en: Record the whole unit as mastered without checking any of the remaining tasks.
options.zh: 未檢查任何餘下工作，就記錄為已掌握整個單元。

options.en: Record only the unfinished tasks and leave out the successful exercise.
options.zh: 只記未完成工作，略去成功的練習。

dialogue.explanationZh: 既承認可驗證的小步驟，也保留未學部分；不能誇大或抹去實際成果。

speaking.en: Small wins can encourage me to continue, while showing which skills still need practice.
speaking.zh: 小成果可鼓勵我繼續，也顯示哪些技巧仍需練習。
speaking.promptZh: 你想肯定小進展，並保留下一步。先聽，再說。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你學新語言，今天能自行寫兩句正確短句，還未能寫完整篇章，但想以此支持繼續練習。用一至兩句英文描述。

examples.en: Writing two correct sentences was a small win for me. I will build on it by practising a short paragraph next.
examples.zh: 自行寫好兩句正確句子，是我的小成果。我會以此為基礎，接着練一小段文章。

examples.en: These small wins help me notice progress, even though I cannot write a whole piece yet. My next step is to connect a few simple ideas.
examples.zh: 即使還不能寫完整文章，這些小成果也幫我留意進展。下一步是連接幾個簡單想法。

writing.selfCheckZh: 把兩句正確句子作可驗證的小成果，不誇成已能寫全文，也不忽略下一步連接想法。

takeaways.en: Small wins helped the trainees continue with the harder tasks.
takeaways.zh: 小成果幫學員繼續面對較難工作。

takeaways.en: A small win is worth noticing without treating it as the whole achievement.
takeaways.zh: 小成果值得留意，但不應把它當作整體成就。

sources.sentence: When she sees the solution, it feels as if the lights come on.

brief.meaningEn: Understanding suddenly becomes clear, as if a dark space has been lit.
brief.meaningZh: 理解突然清晰，彷彿黑暗空間亮起燈。
brief.grammar: it is/was as if the lights come/came on; source plural lights retained; context identifies the idea becoming clear.
brief.register: Figurative understanding image, not a measure of intelligence; do not confuse with actual electrical lighting.
brief.boundaryZh: 想通一點不等於已掌握全部，可能仍需要練習或測試理解。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不是只表示房間變亮；要有理解解釋或解法的線索。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述理解突然建立，以及接着如何鞏固。

listening.promptZh: 這個光線比喻表達甚麼？

options.en: The explanation made a previously unclear idea understandable.
options.zh: 解釋令原本不清楚的概念變得可理解。

options.en: The tutor changed the classroom’s electrical lighting.
options.zh: 導師改了課室的電燈。

options.en: The learner finished every remaining exercise without checking the method.
options.zh: 學習者未核對方法，就完成所有餘下練習。

options.en: The comparison made the reason for the error less clear.
options.zh: 比較令錯誤原因更不清楚。

listening.explanationZh: finally understood 指明理解突然清晰，不是電燈或已完成全部練習。
listening.en: When the tutor drew the two stages side by side, it was as if the lights came on: I finally understood why my first calculation had failed.
listening.zh: 導師把兩階段並排畫出時，彷彿燈突然亮起：我終於明白首次計算為何出錯。

reply.promptEn: What changed when the tutor showed the stages side by side?
reply.promptZh: 導師把兩階段並排展示時，有甚麼改變？

options.en: I could finally see why the first method had failed.
options.zh: 我終於看出第一個方法為何失敗。

options.en: It was as if the lights came on and the link became clear.
options.zh: 彷彿燈突然亮起，連繫變清楚了。

options.en: The comparison helped me understand the part I had missed.
options.zh: 比較幫我理解之前忽略的部分。

options.en: I understood the explanation well enough to try another example.
options.zh: 我理解解釋，可以再試另一例子。

reply.explanationZh: 四句均描述理解轉變；金句不是說無需再練。

scene.promptZh: 學生一直不明白論點與證據的關係，老師畫圖後，他突然懂了，能解釋連繫。哪句貼切？

options.en: It was as if the lights came on when he saw the diagram.
options.zh: 他看見圖時，彷彿燈突然亮起，明白過來。

options.en: The diagram left him unable to see any link between the ideas.
options.zh: 圖讓他無法看出想法之間有任何連繫。

options.en: The only change was that the classroom became physically brighter.
options.zh: 唯一改變是課室實際變亮。

scene.explanationZh: 突然懂及能解釋是理解線索，不是只談燈光。

contrast.promptZh: 哪句是實際燈光，不是本課的理解比喻？

options.en: When I saw the worked example, it was as if the lights came on.
options.zh: 看見示範例子時，彷彿燈突然亮起，我明白過來。

options.en: At sunset, the lights came on in the empty corridor.
options.zh: 日落時，空走廊的燈亮了。

options.en: After the comparison, it felt as though the lights came on in my mind.
options.zh: 比較後，彷彿腦內燈亮起，我想通了。

contrast.explanationZh: 日落、空走廊沒有理解者，是實際照明；示範及腦內則支持比喻。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友看完示範突然想通，就想跳過所有練習，問你有甚麼建議。哪句最好？

options.en: It is great when the lights come on; try a fresh example to check that you can use the idea yourself.
options.zh: 突然想通很好；再試一個新例子，查自己能否運用概念。

options.en: Copy the worked answer as evidence that you can solve a different problem independently.
options.zh: 抄示範答案，當作能獨自解另一題的證據。

options.en: Move on without trying the method because the explanation felt clear at the time.
options.zh: 因當時覺得解釋清楚，就不試方法直接往下學。

dialogue.explanationZh: 理解清晰值得肯定，仍可用新例驗證；抄答案或只憑感覺不能代替運用。

speaking.en: It was as if the lights came on when I saw the link, and now I want to try a new example.
speaking.zh: 看出連繫時，彷彿燈突然亮起，我明白過來；現在想試新例子。
speaking.promptZh: 你想描述理解瞬間，也保留運用練習。先聽，再說。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你一直不懂地圖比例，朋友用教室模型解釋後，你突然明白，想再用另一張地圖練習。用一至兩句英文描述。

examples.en: It was as if the lights came on when my friend used the classroom model. I finally understood the scale and want to practise with another map.
examples.zh: 朋友用課室模型時，彷彿燈突然亮起，我明白過來。我終於懂了比例，想用另一張地圖練習。

examples.en: When I saw the model, it felt as though the lights came on. I will check my understanding by trying a different map on my own.
examples.zh: 看見模型時，彷彿燈突然亮起，我明白過來。我會自己試另一張地圖，檢查理解。

writing.selfCheckZh: 把模型解釋連到突然理解比例，再說新地圖練習；不是電燈亮或已掌握所有地圖技巧。

takeaways.en: It felt as if the lights came on when the connection became clear.
takeaways.zh: 連繫清楚時，彷彿燈突然亮起，我明白過來。

takeaways.en: The lights came on in my mind as the tutor compared the two methods.
takeaways.zh: 導師比較兩個方法時，我腦內彷彿亮起燈，想通了。

sources.sentence: The firm needs rock-solid service standards.

brief.meaningEn: Extremely reliable, firm or secure in the context described.
brief.meaningZh: 在所述情境中，非常可靠、穩固或牢靠。
brief.grammar: rock-solid standards/service/evidence; a rock-solid plan; hyphen before a noun.
brief.register: Conventional strength metaphor and emphatic evaluation; specify what supports the confidence.
brief.boundaryZh: 強調可靠不是保證永不出問題；也不能只因態度自信便叫可靠。
brief.misconceptionZh: 描述證據、服務或安排時，應有穩定表現、檢查或資料支持。
brief.outcomeZh: 能以具體可核實的線索支持高度可靠的評價。

options.en: Consistent accurate service is supported by training and checks.
options.zh: 培訓及檢查支持穩定準確的服務。

options.en: The service depends on one person because no process is shared.
options.zh: 沒有共用流程，所以服務依靠一個人。

options.en: The organisation has stopped checking whether answers are accurate.
options.zh: 機構已停止檢查答案是否準確。

options.en: The description is based only on an impressive new logo.
options.zh: 描述只根據一個出色新標誌。

listening.explanationZh: 換人仍準確及持續檢查是可靠線索，不是單憑外觀或取消流程。
listening.en: Their service became rock-solid after clear training and regular checks: customers received accurate answers even when different staff handled the desk.
listening.zh: 經清楚培訓及定期檢查後，服務變得非常可靠：即使換了櫃台員工，客戶也得到準確答案。

reply.promptEn: Why do you trust the information desk’s service now?
reply.promptZh: 你現在為甚麼信任詢問處服務？

options.en: The staff use clear guidance and check the answers regularly.
options.zh: 員工使用清楚指引，定期核對答案。

options.en: The service is rock-solid across different shifts.
options.zh: 不同更份的服務都非常可靠。

options.en: I have received accurate information from several members of staff.
options.zh: 幾位員工都給我準確資料。

options.en: The training and follow-up make the standard dependable.
options.zh: 培訓及跟進讓服務標準可靠。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都有相關可靠線索；金句是高度評價，不是零問題保證。

scene.promptZh: 團隊的交接表經多次實際使用及核對，換人也能準確接續，錯漏有清楚跟進。哪句有根據？

options.en: The team has built a rock-solid handover process.
options.zh: 團隊已建立非常可靠的交接流程。

options.en: The handover works only when the original writer is present.
options.zh: 交接只在原作者在場時有效。

options.en: The team relies on a confident slogan instead of a tested process.
options.zh: 團隊靠自信口號，而非經測試流程。

scene.explanationZh: 多次使用、核對及換人仍準確，支持穩固流程；不是只靠原作者或口號。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不足以支持 rock-solid service 這個評價？

options.en: Accurate information is delivered consistently across staff changes.
options.zh: 員工更換時，仍穩定提供準確資料。

options.en: A new slogan promises reliability, but performance has not been checked.
options.zh: 新口號承諾可靠，但未檢查表現。

options.en: Regular checks show that the agreed standard is being maintained.
options.zh: 定期檢查顯示議定標準持續維持。

contrast.explanationZh: 口號沒有表現支持，不足以作高度可靠評價。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友看到「rock-solid」宣傳，想立即停止核對服務資料。哪句建議最好？

options.en: Rock-solid is a strong claim, so look for consistent performance and keep the checks that support it.
options.zh: 非常可靠是強烈評價，所以要看穩定表現，並保留支援它的檢查。

options.en: Use the slogan in place of the recent performance records.
options.zh: 用口號取代近期表現紀錄。

options.en: Check only the best shift and leave out the less reliable ones before deciding.
options.zh: 判斷前只查最好更份，略去較不可靠更份。

dialogue.explanationZh: 可靠評價需要完整穩定表現；口號或選擇性資料不足，檢查仍有作用。

speaking.en: A rock-solid service standard depends on clear training and reliable follow-up.
speaking.zh: 非常可靠的服務標準，依靠清楚培訓及可靠跟進。
speaking.promptZh: 你想把高度評價連到具體做法。先聽，再說。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：做校史報告時，你要確認一場展覽的日期，已核對兩份互不抄錄的原始紀錄及同期相片日期，資料一致。你想說證據扎實，而非只靠自信語氣。用一至兩句英文表達。

examples.en: We have rock-solid evidence for the exhibition date: independent records agree, and we have checked the originals.
examples.zh: 我們有非常扎實的證據確認展覽日期：獨立紀錄一致，我們也已核對原件。

examples.en: Our conclusion rests on rock-solid evidence rather than a confident tone; we cross-checked the date against independent records.
examples.zh: 結論以非常扎實的證據為基礎，而非自信語氣；我們已用獨立紀錄互相核對日期。

writing.selfCheckZh: 以獨立紀錄、原件及交叉核對支持扎實證據，不把一句自信宣稱當證據，也不聲稱之後不用再檢查新資料。

takeaways.en: The team needs rock-solid standards that remain clear across staff changes.
takeaways.zh: 團隊需要換人時仍清楚可靠的穩固標準。

takeaways.en: Regular checks helped make the handover process rock-solid.
takeaways.zh: 定期檢查幫交接流程變得非常可靠。

sources.sentence: Without training, customer service can be hit and miss.

brief.meaningEn: Inconsistent in quality or success, with some good results and some poor ones.
brief.meaningZh: 品質或成功情況不穩定，有時好，有時不好。
brief.grammar: service can be hit and miss; hit-and-miss service before a noun; keep both good and poor results in context.
brief.register: Conventional paired phrase, common in British English; not necessarily random failure in every case.
brief.boundaryZh: 不是一直差，也不是每次都好；一次錯誤本身未必足以判斷整體不穩。
brief.misconceptionZh: 要看多次或不同條件的差異，不把少量資料當永久定論。
brief.outcomeZh: 能用對比表現描述不一致，並尋找可改善原因。

options.en: The quality varies rather than staying dependable across visits.
options.zh: 品質有變，不是在不同到訪時都可靠。

options.en: Every visit has produced equally clear and accurate advice.
options.zh: 每次到訪都得到同樣清楚準確的建議。

options.en: The desk has been closed on both days without providing any answer.
options.zh: 兩天詢問處都關閉，沒有提供答案。

options.en: The conflicting advice was resolved before either answer was given.
options.zh: 兩個答案給出前，矛盾已解決。

listening.explanationZh: 清楚答案與矛盾建議形成品質差異，支持不穩定，而非一直好或沒有服務。
listening.en: The help desk was hit and miss: one day I received a clear answer, but the next day a different member of staff gave conflicting advice.
listening.zh: 詢問處服務時好時壞：一天我得到清楚答案，翌日另一位員工卻給矛盾建議。

reply.promptEn: What do you mean when you say the help desk’s service is inconsistent?
reply.promptZh: 你說詢問處服務不穩定，是甚麼意思？

options.en: The advice is useful on some visits but confusing on others.
options.zh: 有時建議有用，有時令人混淆。

options.en: It is hit and miss depending on which shift handles the question.
options.zh: 視乎哪一更處理問題，服務時好時壞。

options.en: Different staff have given me answers that do not match.
options.zh: 不同員工給我的答案不一致。

options.en: I cannot rely on receiving the same clear standard each time.
options.zh: 我不能指望每次都得到同樣清楚的標準。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都可解釋不一致；金句不是所有員工都永遠表現差。

scene.promptZh: 你試用同一借書系統幾次，有時即時完成，有時同樣程序卻漏掉紀錄。哪句合適？

options.en: The system’s performance has been hit and miss.
options.zh: 系統表現一直時好時壞。

options.en: The system has worked reliably on every attempt described.
options.zh: 所述每次嘗試，系統都可靠運作。

options.en: Nobody has tried the system, so there is no result to compare.
options.zh: 沒有人試過系統，所以沒有結果可比較。

scene.explanationZh: 多次不同結果支持不一致；不是每次可靠，也不是未測試。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不足以支持 hit-and-miss service 這個評價？

options.en: Several visits alternate between clear help and conflicting answers.
options.zh: 幾次到訪，有時協助清楚，有時答案矛盾。

options.en: There is one untested opinion with no examples of service performance.
options.zh: 只有一項未核實意見，沒有服務表現例子。

options.en: Records show that quality changes noticeably between shifts.
options.zh: 紀錄顯示更份之間品質明顯不同。

contrast.explanationZh: 判斷不穩定要看表現差異，不能只憑未核實意見。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友看到服務有時好有時差，就只想記錄最差一次作全部結論。哪句建議最好？

options.en: If it is hit and miss, compare both good and poor visits to find where the standard changes.
options.zh: 若服務時好時壞，應比較好與差的到訪經驗，找出標準在哪裏改變。

options.en: Leave out the good visits so the report sounds consistent with the worst one.
options.zh: 略去好的到訪，讓報告完全配合最差一次。

options.en: Average the waiting times alone and ignore whether the answers were accurate.
options.zh: 只計平均等候時間，不理答案是否準確。

dialogue.explanationZh: 要找品質差異，需保留好壞資料及相關標準；只選差例或只看速度不足。

speaking.en: The service is hit and miss, so we should compare the shifts and check the guidance they use.
speaking.zh: 服務時好時壞，所以應比較更份，核對員工使用的指引。
speaking.promptZh: 你想描述不穩定，並找出可檢查的原因。先聽，再說。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你在家依同一食譜做過幾次麵包，有兩次鬆軟，另幾次很實，還未確定原因。你想描述結果不穩，並逐次比較份量及做法。用一至兩句英文表達。

examples.en: My baking results have been hit and miss: some loaves are light, while others are dense. I will compare my measurements and methods before guessing the cause.
examples.zh: 我的烘焙結果一直時好時壞：有些麵包鬆軟，有些很實。猜原因前，我會比較份量及做法。

examples.en: The bread has been hit and miss, so I want to record the ingredients and each step to see why the results vary.
examples.zh: 麵包一直時好時壞，所以我想記錄材料及每一步，了解結果為何不同。

writing.selfCheckZh: 保留有好有差的多次結果，提出記錄比較；未查之前不斷言確切原因，也不說每次都失敗。

takeaways.en: Without clear guidance, the service can be hit and miss.
takeaways.zh: 沒有清楚指引，服務可能時好時壞。

takeaways.en: We compared the shifts to understand the hit-and-miss results.
takeaways.zh: 我們比較不同更份，以了解時好時壞的結果。

sources.sentence: Consistency is the name of the game in public service.

brief.meaningEn: The most important requirement or principle for succeeding in the activity being discussed.
brief.meaningZh: 在所討論活動中成事的最重要要求或原則。
brief.grammar: X is the name of the game in/when + activity; explain why that quality matters.
brief.register: Informal emphatic idiom; the activity need not be a sport or competition.
brief.boundaryZh: 不是活動名稱，也不表示其他因素完全沒有作用；關鍵仍取決於具體目標。
brief.misconceptionZh: 重複一句口號不等於有做法，要連到所需行動及標準。
brief.outcomeZh: 能指出某情境的核心要求，並給出實際理由。

listening.promptZh: 說話者怎樣看待一致性？

options.en: It is a central requirement for providing dependable advice.
options.zh: 它是提供可靠建議的核心要求。

options.en: It is the official title of a game the staff play.
options.zh: 它是員工所玩遊戲的正式名稱。

options.en: It means staff should repeat the same answer even when the facts differ.
options.zh: 它表示即使事實不同，員工也應重複相同答案。

options.en: It is less relevant than making each shift’s guidance look different.
options.zh: 它不及讓各更份指引看來不同那麼重要。

listening.explanationZh: whichever member 支持可靠標準一致；不是遊戲名稱，也不是不顧事實照搬答案。
listening.en: Consistency is the name of the game at the advice desk: people need accurate guidance whichever member of staff they meet.
listening.zh: 在諮詢櫃台，穩定一致是關鍵：無論遇到哪位員工，人們都需要準確指引。

reply.promptEn: What matters most when different staff give advice at the desk?
reply.promptZh: 不同員工在櫃台提供建議時，最重要的是甚麼？

options.en: People should receive accurate guidance across different shifts.
options.zh: 不同更份都應給人準確指引。

options.en: Consistency is the name of the game.
options.zh: 穩定一致是關鍵。

options.en: The team needs an agreed standard rather than answers that depend on who is on duty.
options.zh: 團隊需要議定標準，而非答案隨當值員工改變。

options.en: Clear shared guidance helps everyone work to the same dependable standard.
options.zh: 清楚共用指引，幫大家依同樣可靠標準工作。

reply.explanationZh: 四句均回應核心要求；金句用非正式方式突出重點。

scene.promptZh: 多名義工輪流接報名，最重要是記錄完整一致，避免有人漏掉必要資料。哪句合適？

options.en: Consistency is the name of the game when recording registrations.
options.zh: 記錄報名時，穩定一致是關鍵。

options.en: The main aim is to make each volunteer use a different set of required fields.
options.zh: 主要目的是讓每位義工使用不同必填欄位。

options.en: Consistency is simply the title printed on a board game at the desk.
options.zh: Consistency 只是櫃台桌上遊戲印的名稱。

scene.explanationZh: 必要資料不能因人不同而遺漏，支持一致的核心要求，不是字面遊戲。

contrast.promptZh: 哪句的 name of the game 指實際遊戲名稱，而非本課的核心要求？

options.en: Patience is the name of the game when restoring a delicate old object.
options.zh: 修復精細舊物時，耐心是關鍵。

options.en: The name of the game printed on the box is River Quest.
options.zh: 盒子印的遊戲名稱是 River Quest。

options.en: Clear communication is the name of the game in a handover.
options.zh: 交接時，清楚溝通是關鍵。

contrast.explanationZh: 盒子及名稱 River Quest 是實際標題；耐心、溝通是抽象成事條件。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說「一致是關鍵」，卻想每次都不看資料照回同一句話。哪句提醒最好？

options.en: Consistency is the name of the game, but it means applying a reliable standard to the facts, not ignoring differences.
options.zh: 穩定一致是關鍵，但指按事實使用可靠標準，不是忽略差異。

options.en: Use the same wording for every enquiry before checking what the person is asking.
options.zh: 未查對方問甚麼，就對每個查詢用同一措辭。

options.en: Let each shift invent its own required details so the replies sound more individual.
options.zh: 讓每一更自訂必需資料，令回覆更有個性。

dialogue.explanationZh: 一致是可靠標準，不是無視情況；任由更份改標準也不回應需要。

speaking.en: Consistency is the name of the game, so we need shared guidance and regular checks.
speaking.zh: 穩定一致是關鍵，所以我們需要共用指引及定期檢查。
speaking.promptZh: 你想把核心原則連到實際做法。先聽，再說。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你們數人共同整理口述歷史，最重要是準確記錄受訪者原意，而非趕快做完。用一至兩句英文指出重點及核對方法。

examples.en: Accuracy is the name of the game in this project. We should check the notes against the recordings before sharing them.
examples.zh: 這個項目中，準確是關鍵。分享前，我們應用錄音核對筆記。

examples.en: Accuracy is the name of the game, so we need to preserve what each person meant rather than rush through the interviews.
examples.zh: 準確是關鍵，所以我們需要保留每人的原意，而非匆忙完成訪問。

writing.selfCheckZh: 以訪問原意及錄音核對解釋準確這個核心要求；不把所有活動都套同一要求。

takeaways.en: Reliability is the name of the game when people depend on your information.
takeaways.zh: 人們依靠你的資料時，可靠是關鍵。

takeaways.en: Careful checking is the name of the game in this kind of work.
takeaways.zh: 這類工作中，細心核對是關鍵。

sources.sentence: I made the usual journey on autopilot.

sources.sentence: I made the usual journey on autopilot.

brief.meaningEn: Doing a familiar action automatically, with little conscious attention to each step.
brief.meaningZh: 自動按熟悉習慣行事，很少有意識留意每一步。
brief.grammar: do something on autopilot; go through a routine on autopilot.
brief.register: Conventional aircraft-control metaphor; habitual action can be convenient, but changes may require fresh attention.
brief.boundaryZh: 不是完全失去意識，也不一定每次做錯；本課不指飛機控制系統。
brief.misconceptionZh: 要區分熟悉習慣與刻意重新選擇，尤其原有安排已改時。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述自動習慣，並在情況改變時提出具體核對。

options.en: The speaker followed a familiar routine without noticing the changed schedule.
options.zh: 說話者按熟悉習慣行事，沒有留意時間表已改。

options.en: The speaker checked the new timetable before choosing every book.
options.zh: 說話者選每本書前已查新時間表。

options.en: The school had not changed any classes that afternoon.
options.zh: 學校那天下午沒有改任何課堂。

options.en: The speaker knew the classes had changed but deliberately chose books from the old timetable.
options.zh: 說話者知道課堂已改，卻刻意依舊時間表選書。

listening.explanationZh: old timetable 加 then realised 表示先依習慣、後發現改動；不是已核對新版，也不是知道改動仍刻意用舊版。
listening.en: I packed my bag on autopilot using the old timetable, then realised the afternoon classes had changed.
listening.zh: 我不經思索按舊時間表收書包，之後才發現下午課堂已改。

reply.promptEn: Why did the wrong books end up in your bag?
reply.promptZh: 為甚麼書包裏放了錯的課本？

options.en: I followed the old timetable without noticing the change.
options.zh: 我依舊時間表，沒有留意改動。

options.en: I packed on autopilot and did not check the updated classes.
options.zh: 我依習慣不經思索收書包，沒查更新課堂。

options.en: The familiar routine took over before I looked at the new schedule.
options.zh: 看新時間表前，我先依熟悉習慣做了。

options.en: I had not paused to compare what I usually packed with what I needed that day.
options.zh: 我沒有停下來比較平常收甚麼，以及當天需要甚麼。

reply.explanationZh: 四句均提供錯書的合理原因；金句不是失去意識，也不表示所有習慣都錯。

scene.promptZh: 你照舊複製每週通告，沒有留意本週場地不同，寄出後才察覺。哪句合適？

options.en: I sent the notice on autopilot without checking the changed venue.
options.zh: 我依習慣不經思索寄通告，沒查改了的場地。

options.en: I deliberately checked the new venue and updated the notice before sending it.
options.zh: 我寄出前刻意查新場地，並更新通告。

options.en: I knew the venue had changed but deliberately sent the old location anyway.
options.zh: 我知道場地已改，卻仍刻意寄舊位置。

scene.explanationZh: 照舊複製後才察覺，是未留意的自動習慣；不同於寄前已核對，也不同於明知仍刻意用舊位置。

contrast.promptZh: 哪句是實際飛機系統，而不是人的習慣比喻？

options.en: I made the familiar journey on autopilot and barely thought about the routine.
options.zh: 我不經思索走熟悉路程，幾乎沒留意習慣步驟。

options.en: The aircraft remained on autopilot during that part of the flight.
options.zh: 飛機在那段航程維持自動駕駛。

options.en: She filled in the usual form on autopilot before noticing the new section.
options.zh: 她依習慣填表，之後才察覺新增部分。

contrast.explanationZh: 飛機及航程是實際系統；走路、填表則是自動依習慣的比喻。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友每週複製通告，本週場地已改，問如何避免漏改。哪句最有幫助？

options.en: Avoid sending it on autopilot; check the date and venue against the current plan before you send it.
options.zh: 避免依習慣不經思索寄出；寄前用現行計劃核對日期及場地。

options.en: Copy last week’s notice again and wait for recipients to point out the change.
options.zh: 再次複製上週通告，等收件者指出改動。

options.en: Check only the font and spacing before sending, without comparing the event details.
options.zh: 寄前只查字體及間距，不比較活動資料。

dialogue.explanationZh: 核對容易隨週改變的資料，直接回應習慣漏查；等別人發現或只查格式不足。

speaking.en: I do not want to send this on autopilot, so I will check the current date and venue first.
speaking.zh: 我不想依習慣不經思索寄出，所以會先查現時日期及場地。
speaking.promptZh: 你想提醒自己在熟悉工作中核對改動。先聽，再說。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你每月使用同一報名表，本月新增同意欄位。你想提醒小組不要只照舊填寫，要先讀新版。用一至兩句英文表達。

examples.en: We should not fill in the form on autopilot this month. There is a new consent section, so let us read the updated version first.
examples.zh: 今個月不應只依習慣不經思索填表。新增了同意欄位，所以先讀新版吧。

examples.en: It is easy to complete a familiar form on autopilot, but we need to check the new section before submitting it.
examples.zh: 熟悉的表格很容易只依習慣填寫，但提交前我們需要核對新增部分。

writing.selfCheckZh: 指出熟悉習慣與新增欄位的差別，提出先讀及核對；不要寫成習慣永遠無用或完全失去意識。

takeaways.en: I went through the usual routine on autopilot before noticing the change.
takeaways.zh: 察覺改動前，我先依習慣不經思索做完熟悉程序。

takeaways.en: A familiar task can happen on autopilot unless I pause to check the details.
takeaways.zh: 若不暫停核對細節，熟悉工作可能只依習慣不經思索進行。

brief.meaningEn: Hide or avoid dealing with problems instead of addressing them openly.
brief.meaningZh: 把問題藏起或避開，不坦誠處理。
brief.grammar: sweep a problem/them under the carpet; swept in the past; pronoun them refers to named problems.
brief.register: Conventional concealment idiom; British carpet variant is retained from the source.
brief.boundaryZh: 不只是暫時未有答案；應有掩蓋、刪去或故意不處理問題的線索。
brief.misconceptionZh: 保護私人資料與掩蓋問題並不相同；可保密個人身分，同時記錄及處理問題。
brief.outcomeZh: 能辨認掩蓋與妥善保密，並提出可追蹤處理。

options.en: The manager concealed the problem instead of dealing with it in the review.
options.zh: 經理掩蓋問題，而非在檢討處理。

options.en: The manager recorded the concerns and assigned a follow-up for each one.
options.zh: 經理記錄疑慮，為每項安排跟進。

options.en: The manager protected names while still reporting the pattern and response.
options.zh: 經理保護姓名，同時仍報告模式及回應。

options.en: The manager had received no complaints before the review.
options.zh: 檢討前，經理從沒收到投訴。

listening.explanationZh: 叫人略去反覆投訴，支持掩蓋；不是保護身分同時跟進。
listening.en: Instead of recording the repeated complaints, the manager swept them under the carpet and told staff to leave them out of the review.
listening.zh: 經理沒有記錄反覆投訴，而是把它們掩蓋，叫員工在檢討略去。

reply.promptEn: Why are staff worried about leaving the complaints out of the review?
reply.promptZh: 員工為甚麼擔心在檢討略去投訴？

options.en: The recurring problem will not be visible to the people responsible for fixing it.
options.zh: 負責改善的人會看不見反覆問題。

options.en: They do not want to sweep the problems under the carpet.
options.zh: 他們不想把問題掩蓋而不處理。

options.en: Without a record, it will be harder to check whether anything changes.
options.zh: 沒有紀錄，就更難查有沒有改善。

options.en: The review would miss information needed for a useful response.
options.zh: 檢討會漏掉有效回應所需的資料。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都解釋疑慮；金句不等於必須公開每位投訴者身分。

scene.promptZh: 活動報告有幾次相同失誤，負責人卻要求刪掉相關紀錄，不安排跟進。哪句合適？

options.en: They are sweeping the problems under the carpet.
options.zh: 他們正掩蓋問題，不作處理。

options.en: They are documenting the pattern and assigning clear follow-up actions.
options.zh: 他們正記錄模式，安排清楚跟進。

options.en: They are keeping names private while preserving the problem in the report.
options.zh: 他們保密姓名，同時在報告保留問題。

scene.explanationZh: 刪紀錄且不跟進才是掩蓋；保密姓名但仍處理不相同。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個情況最不符合 sweep problems under the carpet？

options.en: A team removes repeated concerns from the report to avoid discussing them.
options.zh: 團隊從報告刪掉反覆疑慮，避開討論。

options.en: A coordinator protects names but records the problem and assigns a follow-up.
options.zh: 統籌員保護姓名，但記錄問題並安排跟進。

options.en: A manager asks staff to keep known faults out of the review.
options.zh: 經理叫員工把已知缺陷排除於檢討。

contrast.explanationZh: 保密身分仍可處理問題；故意刪去問題或排除檢討才符合本課。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友擔心公開投訴者姓名，便想把整項問題從報告刪除。哪句建議最好？

options.en: We can protect names without sweeping the problem under the carpet; record the issue and agree a confidential follow-up.
options.zh: 我們可保護姓名，而不掩蓋問題；記錄事情，議定保密跟進。

options.en: Delete the whole issue now and rely on people remembering it at the next review.
options.zh: 現在刪整項問題，靠大家下次檢討記得。

options.en: Publish every complainant’s identity before checking which information is actually needed to address the issue.
options.zh: 未查處理問題實際需要哪些資料，就公開每位投訴者身分。

dialogue.explanationZh: 可保護身分，同時保留問題及可追蹤跟進；刪掉整件事或未查需要就公開所有身分，都未兼顧兩者。

speaking.en: We should protect people’s privacy without sweeping the problems under the carpet.
speaking.zh: 我們應保護個人私隱，同時不掩蓋問題。
speaking.promptZh: 你想區分妥善保密與不處理問題。先聽，再說。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：社團每次借器材都有同類漏記，有人怕尷尬想從檢討刪去。你建議不點名，仍記錄流程問題並安排改善。用一至兩句英文表達。

examples.en: We should not sweep the problems under the carpet. We can leave out names while recording the missing entries and agreeing a better process.
examples.zh: 我們不應掩蓋問題。可以不寫姓名，同時記錄漏填及議定較好的流程。

examples.en: Protecting names does not mean sweeping the problem under the carpet; the review still needs a record of the issue and a clear follow-up.
examples.zh: 保護姓名不等於掩蓋問題；檢討仍要有事情紀錄及清楚跟進。

writing.selfCheckZh: 保留不點名與處理流程的兩個要求；不把私隱當刪除全部問題的理由。

takeaways.en: Managers should not sweep the complaints under the carpet.
takeaways.zh: 管理者不應掩蓋投訴而不處理。

takeaways.en: Recording a clear follow-up helps us avoid sweeping problems under the carpet.
takeaways.zh: 記錄清楚跟進，幫我們避免掩蓋問題。

sources.sentence: The supervisor should not brush it off.

brief.meaningEn: Dismiss a concern or request as unimportant, often without considering it properly.
brief.meaningZh: 把疑慮或請求當不重要而打發，常未有妥善考慮。
brief.grammar: brush it off, not brush off it; brush off a concern/brush a concern off; brushed in the past.
brief.register: Common separable phrasal verb; this lesson focuses on dismissing someone’s concern, not brushing dust away.
brief.boundaryZh: 不等於仔細調查後有根據地不同意；也不是每個疑慮都必須被證實才能值得聆聽。
brief.misconceptionZh: 應先了解具體情況，再判斷回應，而不是只因看來小便打發。
brief.outcomeZh: 能辨認輕率回應，並建議合適的釐清或查證。

listening.promptZh: 主管的回應有甚麼問題？

options.en: The concern was dismissed before the relevant details were checked.
options.zh: 相關資料未查，疑慮就被打發。

options.en: The supervisor compared the two dates and explained why they differed.
options.zh: 主管比較兩個日期，解釋差異。

options.en: The supervisor asked each member which deadline they had been given.
options.zh: 主管問每位組員收到哪個限期。

options.en: A clear common deadline had already been confirmed with the whole team.
options.zh: 全組早已確認清楚共同限期。

listening.explanationZh: without checking 支持未妥善考慮便打發，不是已核實並解釋。
listening.en: When I reported the confusing deadline, the supervisor brushed it off as a small detail without checking which dates the team had received.
listening.zh: 我報告限期令人混淆時，主管沒有查團隊收到哪些日期，就當作小事打發。

reply.promptEn: Why were you dissatisfied with the response to the deadline concern?
reply.promptZh: 你為甚麼不滿對限期疑慮的回應？

options.en: The supervisor did not check the conflicting dates.
options.zh: 主管沒有查矛盾日期。

options.en: The supervisor brushed it off before understanding the confusion.
options.zh: 主管未了解混淆，就輕率打發。

options.en: Calling it minor left the team unsure which date to follow.
options.zh: 只說是小事，讓團隊仍不知依哪個日期。

options.en: I needed a clear answer, not just reassurance that the issue was small.
options.zh: 我需要清楚答案，不只是說事情小的安慰。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都解釋不滿；金句不是禁止有根據地不同意，而是未考慮就打發。

scene.promptZh: 學生說兩份通告日期不同，負責人只說「別想太多」，沒有看通告。哪句有根據？

options.en: The concern was brushed off without checking the notices.
options.zh: 疑慮未經核對通告，就被輕率打發。

options.en: The notices were compared and a corrected date was clearly shared.
options.zh: 通告已被比較，正確日期也清楚公布。

options.en: The student’s question was investigated before the reply was given.
options.zh: 回覆前，學生的問題已被查清。

scene.explanationZh: 未看資料便叫人別想太多，支持打發；不是先查後回。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個情況最不符合 brush it off 這裏的意思？

options.en: A concern is called trivial before anyone asks what happened.
options.zh: 未問發生甚麼，就把疑慮說成瑣碎。

options.en: The team checks the evidence and explains why the reported issue does not apply in this case.
options.zh: 團隊查證據，解釋為何所報問題不適用於此個案。

options.en: A request is dismissed without reading the details.
options.zh: 未讀詳情，就把請求打發。

contrast.explanationZh: 查證後有根據地回應不同意見，不等於未考慮就輕率打發。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友覺得參加者提出的時間混淆很小，想直接叫對方別擔心。哪句建議最好？

options.en: Do not brush it off; ask which dates they saw and compare them before replying.
options.zh: 不要輕率打發；先問對方看過哪些日期，核對後才回覆。

options.en: Send reassurance about the organiser’s experience before reading the conflicting notices.
options.zh: 未讀矛盾通告，先寄一段主辦者多有經驗的安心說話。

options.en: Use the shorter notice as the answer without checking which version is current.
options.zh: 未查哪版最新，就以較短通告作答案。

dialogue.explanationZh: 先釐清日期及版本，才能有效回應；安心說話或按長短選版本不能解決混淆。

speaking.en: I do not want to brush the concern off; let us check the details before we respond.
speaking.zh: 我不想輕率打發這項疑慮；回應前先查詳情吧。
speaking.promptZh: 你想尊重疑慮，也保留查證。先聽，再說。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：工作坊參加者說場地太吵，難聽清指示。有人想說只是小事，你建議先了解哪個位置及時段最受影響，再調整。用一至兩句英文表達。

examples.en: We should not brush the concern off. Let us ask where the noise is worst and check how we can make the instructions clearer.
examples.zh: 我們不應輕率打發疑慮。先問哪個位置噪音最嚴重，再查如何令指示更清楚。

examples.en: Instead of brushing it off as a small issue, we should find out when people cannot hear and consider a quieter arrangement.
examples.zh: 與其當作小事打發，我們應了解甚麼時候大家聽不清，並考慮較安靜安排。

writing.selfCheckZh: 回應噪音及指示需要，先了解再調整；不把聆聽疑慮當作已證實所有原因。

takeaways.en: The supervisor should not brush the concern off without checking it.
takeaways.zh: 主管不應未查便輕率打發疑慮。

takeaways.en: She brushed it off as unimportant before reading the details.
takeaways.zh: 未讀詳情，她就把事情當不重要而打發。

brief.meaningEn: Fail to reach an expected or required amount or standard.
brief.meaningZh: 未達預期或所需的數量、程度或標準。
brief.grammar: fall short of + target/standard; fall short by + amount; fell short in the past.
brief.register: Conventional idiom labelled as such in Cambridge and Oxford; the PDF’s phrasal-verb label is preserved in provenance.
brief.boundaryZh: 未達標不等於完全沒有成果，也不是一定只差很少；差距需看資料。
brief.misconceptionZh: 先清楚目標及實績，才能描述短缺；不要把評價推成人的整體價值。
brief.outcomeZh: 能準確比較結果與要求，並指出需要補足的部分。

options.en: It produced useful replies but did not reach the required number.
options.zh: 它有有用回覆，但未達所需數量。

options.en: It reached forty replies exactly.
options.zh: 它剛好收到四十份。

options.en: It received no replies from any family.
options.zh: 它沒有收到任何家庭回覆。

options.en: It exceeded the target by ten replies.
options.zh: 它超出目標十份。

listening.explanationZh: 三十少於四十，支持未達標；有三十份回覆，不是毫無成果。
listening.en: We needed forty replies, but received thirty, so the survey fell short of its target despite a useful response from many families.
listening.zh: 我們需要四十份回覆，卻只收到三十份，所以調查未達目標，儘管不少家庭提供了有用回應。

reply.promptEn: How did the survey do against the target of forty replies?
reply.promptZh: 調查相對四十份回覆的目標，表現怎樣？

options.en: We received thirty, so we still needed ten more.
options.zh: 我們收到三十份，所以仍差十份。

options.en: It fell short of the target, though the replies we received were useful.
options.zh: 它未達目標，但收到的回覆有用。

options.en: The total was below the number we had planned for.
options.zh: 總數低於原定數量。

options.en: We had a helpful response, but not enough replies to meet the target.
options.zh: 我們有有用回應，但數量不足以達標。

reply.explanationZh: 四句均準確表達差距及已有成果；金句不等於完全失敗或毫無回覆。

scene.promptZh: 小組需籌二百英鎊材料費，實收一百七十英鎊，已有進展但仍欠三十英鎊。哪句準確？

options.en: The total fell short of the target by thirty pounds.
options.zh: 總數比目標少三十英鎊。

options.en: The group exceeded the target by thirty pounds.
options.zh: 小組超出目標三十英鎊。

options.en: The group received no contribution towards the materials.
options.zh: 小組沒有收到任何材料費捐助。

scene.explanationZh: 一百七十低於二百，差三十；不是超出或毫無貢獻。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個推論不宜只憑 fall short 作出？

options.en: A result does not reach an expected level.
options.zh: 結果未達預期程度。

options.en: There must have been no useful achievement at all.
options.zh: 必定完全沒有有用成果。

options.en: The size of the gap needs further information.
options.zh: 差距大小需要更多資料。

contrast.explanationZh: 未達標與部分成果可並存，片語本身不提供差距數字。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說調查未達目標，就想刪掉已收到的有用回覆。哪句回應最好？

options.en: It fell short, but the existing replies still matter; report the gap and decide whether more responses are needed.
options.zh: 它未達標，但現有回覆仍重要；報告差距，再決定是否需要更多回應。

options.en: Remove the thirty replies from the report because only a completed target is worth recording.
options.zh: 從報告刪掉三十份回覆，因只有達標才值得記錄。

options.en: Change the original target to thirty without explaining the difference.
options.zh: 不解釋差異，就把原目標改成三十。

dialogue.explanationZh: 誠實保留成果與短缺，才能評估下一步；刪成果或無交代改目標都不準確。

speaking.en: The result fell short of the target, but we should report both the useful progress and the remaining gap.
speaking.zh: 結果未達目標，但我們應同時報告有用進展及餘下差距。
speaking.promptZh: 你想準確評價未達標，而不抹去成果。先聽，再說。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：社團歷史摘要已整理重要日期，但課程要求列明資料來源，你還未補上，所以未達標。你想保留有用研究，補好參考資料。用一至兩句英文描述差距及下一步。

examples.en: Our summary fell short of the required standard because it lacked clear sources. We will add the references without discarding the useful research.
examples.zh: 摘要因欠清楚來源而未達所需標準。我們會補參考資料，不丟棄有用研究。

examples.en: The draft falls short of the course requirements, although the dates are useful. We should keep that research and document where the information came from.
examples.zh: 草稿未達課程要求，但日期有用。我們應保留研究，並記錄資料來自哪裏。

writing.selfCheckZh: 把欠來源連到未達明示標準，同時保留重要日期的研究成果；不把未達標寫成完全沒有價值。

takeaways.en: The first proposal fell short of the required standard.
takeaways.zh: 首個建議未達所需標準。

takeaways.en: We can acknowledge progress while recognising that the result falls short.
takeaways.zh: 我們可肯定進展，同時承認結果仍未達標。

brief.grammar: live up to expectations; lived up to high expectations; live up to + noun phrase is inseparable.
brief.register: Evaluative phrasal verb, labelled as such by Cambridge and Oxford; expectations may be reasonable or excessive.
brief.boundaryZh: 不是只說受到讚賞，也不表示所有期望都合理；本課比較表現與先前要求。
brief.misconceptionZh: 要先了解期望內容，不能把一次結果當成人的全部價值。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述表現是否符合期望，並把要求與合理支援連起來。

options.en: Pressure to perform as well as others expected after the earlier success.
options.zh: 在之前成功後，受到要達到別人期待的表現壓力。

options.en: They had already matched the earlier team’s standards before setting any goals.
options.zh: 未訂任何目標前，他們已達到前隊標準。

options.en: No expectations about performance had been formed.
options.zh: 大家尚未對表現有任何期望。

options.en: A decision to copy the earlier team’s goals without discussing their current needs.
options.zh: 不討論現有需要，便決定照抄之前小組的目標。

listening.explanationZh: felt pressure to 是面對要求，並非已達標；agreed clear goals 表示有討論設定。
listening.en: The new team felt pressure to live up to high expectations after the club’s earlier success, so the coach agreed clear goals for their first season.
listening.zh: 社團之前成功後，新隊感到要符合高期望的壓力，所以教練議定首季清楚目標。

reply.promptEn: Why did the coach want to agree clear goals with the new team?
reply.promptZh: 教練為甚麼想與新隊議定清楚目標？

options.en: The earlier success had led people to expect a lot from them.
options.zh: 之前成功令大家對新隊有很大期望。

options.en: They felt pressure to live up to high expectations.
options.zh: 他們感到要符合高期望的壓力。

options.en: Clear goals could make the demands more concrete and manageable.
options.zh: 清楚目標可讓要求更具體，也較可應付。

options.en: The team needed to understand what a successful first season would mean.
options.zh: 小組需要明白怎樣才算首季成功。

reply.explanationZh: 四句均合理解釋定目標；金句不是所有期待都應無條件接受。

scene.promptZh: 新劇評價原本很高，觀眾看完後覺得實際演出確實達到原先高標準。哪句準確？

options.en: The performance lived up to high expectations.
options.zh: 演出符合了大家的高期望。

options.en: The performance fell below the standard the audience had expected.
options.zh: 演出低於觀眾預期標準。

options.en: The audience had no earlier expectations to compare it with.
options.zh: 觀眾沒有先前期望可作比較。

scene.explanationZh: 題目明言實際演出達到原先標準，才可說 lived up to，而非只因受關注。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個推論不宜只憑 live up to high expectations 得出？

options.en: Performance is being compared with demanding expectations.
options.zh: 正把表現與很高期望比較。

options.en: Every expectation placed on the person must be fair or reasonable.
options.zh: 加諸那個人的每項期望都必定公平合理。

options.en: Context is needed to know what those expectations involve.
options.zh: 要有情境才知道期望涉及甚麼。

contrast.explanationZh: 片語描述符合要求，不替要求是否公平作保證；需分別檢視。

dialogue.promptZh: 新隊員說別人期望很高，便打算直接照抄上一屆訓練量，不問自身能力。哪句較有幫助？

options.en: Trying to live up to high expectations is understandable, but agree suitable goals and support for this team first.
options.zh: 想符合高期望可以理解，但先為這隊議定合適目標及支援。

options.en: Use the earlier workload as the plan before checking the new players’ experience.
options.zh: 未查新球員經驗，就用之前工作量作計劃。

options.en: Treat one difficult result as enough evidence about each player’s long-term value.
options.zh: 只憑一次不理想結果，就判斷每位球員長遠價值。

dialogue.explanationZh: 把要求具體化並配合能力及支援，比照抄負擔或單次評價更有用。

speaking.en: We want to live up to high expectations, but we need clear goals and suitable support.
speaking.zh: 我們想符合高期望，但需要清楚目標及合適支援。
speaking.promptZh: 你想承認期待，也提出達成所需條件。先聽，再說。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：社區科學工作坊的宣傳令參加者期望很高，但很多人是初學者。你想準備清楚指示、合適活動及充足時間，回應期望。用一至兩句英文說明計劃。

examples.en: The workshop needs to live up to high expectations after the publicity. We should prepare clear instructions and activities that suit beginners.
examples.zh: 宣傳後，工作坊需要符合大家的高期望。我們應準備清楚指示，以及適合初學者的活動。

examples.en: To live up to high expectations, we need enough time for beginners to try the activities, rather than simply add more impressive demonstrations.
examples.zh: 要符合高期望，我們需要足夠時間讓初學者嘗試活動，而非只加入更多出色示範。

writing.selfCheckZh: 把高期望連到初學者需要及實際活動安排，不保證所有人必定滿意，也不以華麗示範代替參與時間。

takeaways.en: The performance lived up to high expectations after careful preparation.
takeaways.zh: 細心準備後，演出符合了大家的高期望。

takeaways.en: Young players may need support as they try to live up to expectations.
takeaways.zh: 年輕球員努力符合期望時，可能需要支援。

lessons.titleEn: a weight or heavy load on someone’s shoulders

target.pattern: \ba (?:(?:heavy )?weight on (?:my|your|his|her|our|their)|heavy load on the family['’]s) shoulders\b

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: The deadline felt like a weight on their shoulders.

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 10 to 16 Part 3.docx
sources.locatorNote: DOCX table 151, row 2; page refers to the locally rendered PDF recorded in the intake summary.
sources.sentence: Tuition became a heavy load on the family's shoulders.
sources.expression: heavy load on the family's shoulders

brief.meaningEn: A responsibility, worry or financial pressure that feels burdensome; both weight and heavy load use physical burden to describe the pressure felt by a person or family.
brief.meaningZh: 令人感到沉重的責任、擔憂或經濟壓力；weight 和 heavy load 都借用身體負重來形容個人或家庭承受的壓力。
brief.grammar: Feel like/become a weight on someone’s shoulders; a heavy load on the family’s shoulders names the same burden metaphor in the source. Explain the responsibility, worry or cost and who must bear it; the family’s is a singular possessive, shoulders remains plural.
brief.register: A student discussing shared responsibility with teammates, or a parent explaining an unexpected bill to another family member, can use this neutral-to-emphatic bodily metaphor.
brief.boundaryZh: 這裏不是量度實物重量；heavy load 可指經濟壓力，並不證明家庭完全無法應付，也不等於負擔一定由別人強加。
brief.misconceptionZh: 要說明具體責任或費用及由誰承受；描述沉重感不等於已經失敗或沒有商量支援的餘地。
brief.outcomeZh: 能以具體責任、擔憂或費用說明肩上重擔，區分比喻壓力與實際重量。

options.en: The broad responsibility and unclear division of work.
options.zh: 責任廣泛，加上分工不明。

options.en: A heavy object was being carried during the exhibition.
options.zh: 展覽期間有人搬着重物。

options.en: The work had been fully reassigned and she had no remaining responsibility.
options.zh: 工作已全數改派，她沒有餘下責任。

options.en: The roles had all been confirmed before she accepted the task.
options.zh: 她接工作前，所有分工都已確認。

listening.explanationZh: 負責整個展覽及其他角色未清，是責任負擔線索，不是實際搬重物。
listening.en: Being responsible for the whole exhibition felt like a weight on her shoulders, especially while the other roles were still unclear.
listening.zh: 負責整個展覽令她感到肩負沉重壓力，尤其其他分工仍不清楚。

reply.promptEn: Why does organising the exhibition feel so demanding for her?
reply.promptZh: 安排展覽為甚麼令她覺得壓力很大？

options.en: She is responsible for the whole event while other roles remain unclear.
options.zh: 她負責整項活動，其他角色卻仍不清楚。

options.en: It feels like a weight on her shoulders because too many decisions depend on her.
options.zh: 太多決定依靠她處理，所以她感到肩負沉重壓力。

options.en: Too many decisions are coming to her without an agreed division of work.
options.zh: 沒有議定分工，太多決定都落到她身上。

options.en: She cannot plan her own part confidently while the other responsibilities remain uncertain.
options.zh: 其他責任未清，令她難有把握安排自己的部分。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都能合理說明壓力或所缺條件；金句不是她沒有任何能力。

scene.promptZh: 住家的屋頂突然要維修，費用超過這家人的備用積蓄，令他們擔心接下來的日常開支。哪句最貼切？

options.en: The unexpected repair became a heavy load on the family's shoulders.
options.zh: 突如其來的維修費成了這家人肩上的沉重負擔。

options.en: The repair has no effect on the family’s finances because they had savings.
options.zh: 因為家人有積蓄，維修費對他們的財政毫無影響。

options.en: The family is concerned only about the physical weight of the roof tiles.
options.zh: 這家人只擔心屋頂瓦片的實際重量。

scene.explanationZh: 維修費超出備用積蓄，家人擔心後續開支；這是比喻經濟壓力，並非瓦片重量。

contrast.promptZh: 哪句是實際負重，而不是本課的責任比喻？

options.en: The approaching deadline felt like a weight on their shoulders.
options.zh: 限期逼近，令他們感到肩負沉重壓力。

options.en: The loaded backpack put a heavy weight on his shoulders during the walk.
options.zh: 步行時，裝滿的背包把沉重負荷壓在他肩上。

options.en: Managing the whole project was a weight on her shoulders.
options.zh: 管理整個項目，是她肩上的沉重責任。

contrast.explanationZh: 背包及步行有實際負重；限期及管理項目是責任或擔心。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴覺得展覽責任沉重，別人想只叫她「別擔心」而不談分工。哪句更有幫助？

options.en: If it feels like a weight on her shoulders, ask which decisions can be shared and make the roles clear.
options.zh: 如果她感到肩負沉重壓力，就問哪些決定可分擔，並釐清角色。

options.en: Repeat the reassurance and leave every decision assigned to her as before.
options.zh: 重複安心說話，仍把每個決定照舊留給她。

options.en: Reassign tasks in the group chat before asking what support she actually needs.
options.zh: 未問實際所需支援，就在群組改派工作。

dialogue.explanationZh: 先了解負擔及商議分工，才能對應需要；只安慰或未問便重派不足。

speaking.en: The responsibility feels like a weight on my shoulders, so I want to agree a clearer division of work.
speaking.zh: 這份責任令我感到肩負沉重壓力，所以我想議定更清楚分工。
speaking.promptZh: 你想說清壓力來源，並提出可討論支援。先聽，再說。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：選擇升學課程是你要作的重要決定，家人的期待令你覺得責任沉重。你想先找導師比較路向，而不是讓別人替你決定。用一至兩句英文表達。

examples.en: Choosing my course feels like a weight on my shoulders because the decision matters so much. I want guidance to compare the options before deciding.
examples.zh: 選課程令我感到肩負沉重壓力，因為決定很重要。我想先取得指導、比較選項，再決定。

examples.en: The expectations feel like a weight on my shoulders, so I will discuss the different routes with my tutor while keeping the final choice my own.
examples.zh: 這些期待令我感到肩負沉重壓力，所以我會與導師討論不同路向，同時保留自己作最後選擇。

writing.selfCheckZh: 描述重要決定及期待帶來的壓力，提出比較路向的支援，不把所有決定交出，也不說自己完全無能力。

takeaways.en: Having to make every final decision became a weight on her shoulders.
takeaways.zh: 每個最後決定都要她作，成為她肩上重擔。

takeaways.en: The repair bill became a heavy load on the family's shoulders, even though they had some savings.
takeaways.zh: 即使家人有些積蓄，維修費仍成為他們肩上的沉重負擔。

lessons.titleEn: tie their entire self-worth to success
lessons.titleZh: 把全部自我價值繫於成敗

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Athletes should not tie their entire self-worth to success.
sources.expression: tie their entire self-worth to success

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Students should not tie their self-worth to results.

brief.meaningEn: Base one’s whole judgement of personal value on achievement or outcomes.
brief.meaningZh: 只以成就或結果，判斷自己整體個人價值。
brief.grammar: tie one’s entire self-worth to success/results; tied in the past; tying with -ying.
brief.register: Figurative dependency image; distinguish caring about achievement from treating it as the whole measure of a person.
brief.boundaryZh: 重視成績不一定等於以成績定全部價值；要有「只有成功才值得」等線索。
brief.misconceptionZh: 可努力改善表現，同時承認人還有關係、品格及其他貢獻，不把失敗變成人格定論。
brief.outcomeZh: 能辨認全有全無的價值判斷，並分開結果與整體自我評價。

listening.promptZh: 哪種判斷令一次被拒影響如此大？

options.en: He was treating one outcome as a judgement of his whole personal value.
options.zh: 他把一次結果當作整體個人價值的判斷。

options.en: He separated the rejected application from his value in other parts of life.
options.zh: 他把申請被拒與生活其他方面的價值分開。

options.en: He regarded the application as one useful experience without a wider personal judgement.
options.zh: 他把申請視為一項有用經驗，沒有更廣的自我判斷。

options.en: He was concerned only about the practical application fee.
options.zh: 他只在乎實際申請費。

listening.explanationZh: nothing of value 把一次結果擴至全人價值，不只是正常失望或費用問題。
listening.en: He had tied his entire self-worth to success, so one rejected application made him feel he had nothing of value to offer.
listening.zh: 他把全部自我價值繫於成功，所以一次申請被拒，就令他覺得自己沒有任何有價值的貢獻。

reply.promptEn: Why did one rejected application affect his view of himself so strongly?
reply.promptZh: 為甚麼一次申請被拒，就如此影響他對自己的看法？

options.en: He was using that result as the main test of his value as a person.
options.zh: 他用那個結果作個人價值的主要尺度。

options.en: He had tied his entire self-worth to success.
options.zh: 他把全部自我價值繫於成功。

options.en: He struggled to see his other strengths once the application failed.
options.zh: 申請失敗後，他難以看見自己的其他長處。

options.en: He treated rejection as saying something about his whole worth, not only this opportunity.
options.zh: 他把被拒看成對整體價值的判斷，不只關乎這次機會。

reply.explanationZh: 四句均解釋全人價值被一項結果牽動；不是說在乎申請本身有錯。

scene.promptZh: 學生說：「我只有得最高分才有價值，其他關係與貢獻都不算。」哪句最貼切？

options.en: She is tying her entire self-worth to results.
options.zh: 她正把全部自我價值繫於結果。

options.en: She values the result while keeping it separate from her worth as a person.
options.zh: 她重視結果，同時把它與個人價值分開。

options.en: She is only comparing the marks to decide which topic needs more practice.
options.zh: 她只在比較分數，決定哪個課題多練。

scene.explanationZh: 只有最高分才有價值明確超出一般重視成績，是整體自我評價被綁住。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不足以說某人 ties their entire self-worth to success？

options.en: They say one failed result makes every other contribution worthless.
options.zh: 他們說一次失敗令其他貢獻全無價值。

options.en: They want to improve a result but still value their relationships and other qualities.
options.zh: 他們想改善結果，仍珍惜關係及其他特質。

options.en: They believe they deserve respect only when they win.
options.zh: 他們相信只有勝出才值得尊重。

contrast.explanationZh: 努力改進與保留其他價值並存，不足以指全盤自我價值繫於成敗。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友申請被拒，說連一向幫同伴的貢獻也不算，問自己是否沒有價值。哪句最好？

options.en: Try not to tie your entire self-worth to success in one application; we can review it while recognising the other things you contribute.
options.zh: 盡量別把全部自我價值繫於一次申請成功；可檢討申請，同時肯定其他貢獻。

options.en: Review only the rejection and leave out the strengths that did not appear in the application.
options.zh: 只檢視被拒，略去申請沒呈現的長處。

options.en: Stop discussing the application altogether rather than separating its result from your value.
options.zh: 完全停止談申請，而不把結果與個人價值分開。

dialogue.explanationZh: 可以檢討具體結果，同時保留其他價值；不必抹去長處，也不用逃避一切回顧。

speaking.en: I can care about my work without tying my entire self-worth to success.
speaking.zh: 我可重視工作，而不把全部自我價值繫於成功。
speaking.promptZh: 你想分開努力改善與全盤自我評價。先聽，再說。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你考得第一，很開心，但不想以後只有再得第一才覺得自己有價值。你也珍惜友情及幫同伴的貢獻。用一至兩句英文肯定成績，同時保留其他自我價值。

examples.en: I am proud of this result, but I do not want to tie my entire self-worth to success. I also value my friendships and the help I give others.
examples.zh: 我為這次成績自豪，但不想把全部自我價值繫於成功。我也珍惜友情，以及自己給別人的協助。

examples.en: Rather than tying my self-worth to results, I can celebrate this achievement while remembering my relationships and contributions beyond the exam.
examples.zh: 與其把自我價值繫於結果，我可慶祝這次成就，同時記得考試以外的關係及貢獻。

writing.selfCheckZh: 承認真實成功與開心，同時保留友情及貢獻；不是否定所有成績，也不說只有再第一才有價值。

takeaways.en: We should not tie our entire self-worth to success in one area.
takeaways.zh: 我們不應把全部自我價值繫於某一方面的成功。

takeaways.en: She learnt to value her effort without tying her self-worth to results.
takeaways.zh: 她學會重視努力，而不把自我價值繫於結果。

lessons.titleZh: 讓才能開路而非困住自己

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Talent should be a springboard, not a cage.

brief.meaningEn: An ability should create opportunities rather than restrict someone to a single required path.
brief.meaningZh: 能力應帶來機會，而非把人局限於唯一必走的路。
brief.grammar: talent/ability should be a springboard, not a cage; paired concrete images form a contextual contrast.
brief.register: Figurative contrast, not a fixed technical term; springboard enables movement while cage restricts choice.
brief.boundaryZh: 不是反對練習或承諾，而是反對只因擅長某項便失去其他選擇。
brief.misconceptionZh: 要聽當事人興趣及目標，不把他人的投資或稱讚當必須終身從事的理由。
brief.outcomeZh: 能承認才能帶來選擇，同時保留探索別路的權利。

options.en: Ability can enable choices rather than dictate one compulsory path.
options.zh: 能力可帶來選擇，而非規定唯一必走的路。

options.en: The student should abandon every skill she has already developed.
options.zh: 學生應放棄已發展的每項技巧。

options.en: Being skilled means her future subject has already been chosen for her.
options.zh: 有技巧就表示未來科目已替她選好。

options.en: The teacher is comparing pieces of sports equipment in a real room.
options.zh: 老師正在真實房間比較運動器材。

listening.explanationZh: open options 與 without forcing 明確對比機會及局限，不是放棄技巧或真的器材。
listening.en: Her teacher said talent should be a springboard, not a cage: being good at maths could open options without forcing her to choose only mathematics.
listening.zh: 老師說才能應讓人開路，而非把人困住：擅長數學可帶來選擇，但不應迫她只選數學。

reply.promptEn: How should we think about a student’s strong ability when discussing future study?
reply.promptZh: 討論升學時，我們應怎樣看學生的強項？

options.en: It can give the student more possibilities without deciding everything for them.
options.zh: 它可給學生更多可能，不必替他決定一切。

options.en: It should be a springboard, not a cage.
options.zh: 它應讓人開路，而非把人困住。

options.en: We should consider the student’s interests as well as the subjects they do well in.
options.zh: 我們應考慮學生興趣，也看擅長科目。

options.en: Existing strengths can support exploration of more than one route.
options.zh: 現有強項可支援探索不止一條路。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都保留能力與選擇的關係；金句不表示沒有責任或不用練習。

scene.promptZh: 學生很擅長鋼琴，卻也想讀設計；導師願意幫她比較路向，不因舊有成績限制選擇。哪句合適？

options.en: Her talent can be a springboard, not a cage.
options.zh: 她的才能可讓她開路，而非把她困住。

options.en: Her earlier achievement means music must be her only future subject.
options.zh: 她之前成績表示音樂必須是唯一未來科目。

options.en: She must stop using everything she learnt in music before exploring design.
options.zh: 探索設計前，她必須停止運用所有音樂所學。

scene.explanationZh: 比較路向及不受舊成績局限，符合機會而非禁錮；不必抹去原有學習。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不符合 a springboard, not a cage 的原意？

options.en: A skill supports new opportunities while leaving room for personal choice.
options.zh: 技巧支援新機會，同時保留個人選擇。

options.en: Past success is used as the sole reason to forbid another field the student wants to explore.
options.zh: 只因過去成功，就禁止學生探索另一個想嘗試的領域。

options.en: A mentor helps someone consider how existing strengths could support different routes.
options.zh: 導師幫人考慮現有強項可怎樣支援不同路向。

contrast.explanationZh: 用成功禁止別路正是 cage 的限制面，與整句倡議相反。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「家人替我安排過很多音樂課，所以我不能再考慮設計。」哪句較有幫助？

options.en: Your ability can be a springboard, not a cage; discuss your interests and compare the actual routes before deciding.
options.zh: 你的能力可讓你開路，而非困住你；先討論興趣，比較實際路向，再決定。

options.en: Choose only the route with the longest past training record before considering your current interests.
options.zh: 未考慮現時興趣，就只選過去培訓最久的路。

options.en: Drop all music practice immediately before finding out what either course involves.
options.zh: 未了解兩個課程，就立即停掉全部音樂練習。

dialogue.explanationZh: 比較興趣及實際路向，才可保留選擇；只看過去投入或立即全棄，都未完整考慮。

speaking.en: I want my talent to be a springboard, not a cage, while I explore the options that interest me.
speaking.zh: 探索感興趣選項時，我想才能為我開路，而非把我困住。
speaking.promptZh: 你想承認強項，也保留探索選擇。先聽，再說。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你擅長統籌，所以小組每次都要求你做組長；這次你想當普通組員，學習新的技術工作。用一至兩句英文說明強項應增加選擇，而非困在固定角色。

examples.en: My organising ability should be a springboard, not a cage. This time I want to contribute as a team member and learn a new technical skill.
examples.zh: 我的統籌能力應為我開路，而非把我困住。這次我想以組員身分貢獻，學習新的技術技巧。

examples.en: I want my strengths to be a springboard, not a cage, so I would like to try a different role rather than lead every project.
examples.zh: 我想強項為我開路，而非困住我，所以想嘗試不同角色，而非每次項目都做領導。

writing.selfCheckZh: 把統籌強項與嘗試技術角色連起來，不把願意轉角色說成放棄所有責任，也不抹去原有能力。

takeaways.en: Her drawing ability became a springboard, not a cage, when she began exploring unfamiliar subjects.
takeaways.zh: 開始探索陌生題材時，她的繪畫能力成為跳板，而非牢籠。

takeaways.en: Her ability became a springboard, not a cage, as she explored different courses.
takeaways.zh: 她探索不同課程時，能力為她開路，而非把她困住。

lessons.titleZh: 看似直達成功的通行證

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: A degree alone is not a golden ticket to a good job.

brief.meaningEn: An advantage or opportunity regarded as a route to success, sometimes as though success were guaranteed.
brief.meaningZh: 被視為通往成功的優勢或機會，有時被當作成功保證。
brief.grammar: a golden ticket to + opportunity/outcome; often used negatively to challenge an assumed guarantee.
brief.register: Conventional prize-access metaphor; whether it truly assures success depends on the context.
brief.boundaryZh: 不是每項資格都沒有價值，而是單靠它未必足夠；否定保證不等於否定優勢。
brief.misconceptionZh: 要分清提高機會與確保結果，並看其他要求。
brief.outcomeZh: 能承認資格有用，同時指出成功所需的其他條件。

options.en: It can help, but does not by itself assure the job outcome.
options.zh: 它可有幫助，但單靠它不能保證工作結果。

options.en: It guarantees the job without any practical assessment.
options.zh: 它保證獲聘，不需實際評估。

options.en: It has no relevance to the application at all.
options.zh: 它與申請完全無關。

options.en: It replaces the need to explain or demonstrate any work.
options.zh: 它取代解釋或展示作品的需要。

listening.explanationZh: useful 承認價值，but not 及 still need 否定單靠證書便足夠。
listening.en: The certificate is useful, but it is not a golden ticket to the job; applicants still need to show practical work and communicate clearly.
listening.zh: 證書有用，但不是直達這份工作的通行證；申請者仍需展示實際作品，也要清楚溝通。

reply.promptEn: Why should applicants prepare examples of their work as well as a certificate?
reply.promptZh: 申請者為甚麼除了證書，也應準備作品例子？

options.en: The employer needs evidence of practical ability too.
options.zh: 僱主也需要實際能力的證據。

options.en: A certificate alone is not a golden ticket to the job.
options.zh: 單靠證書不是直達工作的通行證。

options.en: The selection includes how well they can explain what they have done.
options.zh: 甄選也看他們能否清楚解釋做過甚麼。

options.en: The qualification helps, but other requirements still matter.
options.zh: 資格有幫助，但其他要求仍重要。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都解釋準備實例的需要；金句沒有說證書毫無價值。

scene.promptZh: 畢業生有相關學位，職位卻也要求作品集及面試，不能只交學歷便確定獲聘。哪句準確？

options.en: The degree is not a golden ticket to the position.
options.zh: 學位不是直達這個職位的通行證。

options.en: The degree makes the portfolio and interview requirements irrelevant.
options.zh: 學位令作品集及面試要求不再相關。

options.en: The degree cannot offer any advantage in a relevant application.
options.zh: 相關申請中，學位不可能提供任何優勢。

scene.explanationZh: 有用但不單獨確保結果；不能因此取消其他要求，或推成學位全無優勢。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個推論最不宜由 not a golden ticket 得出？

options.en: The advantage alone does not guarantee the outcome.
options.zh: 單靠該優勢不保證結果。

options.en: The advantage must have no value whatsoever.
options.zh: 該優勢必定完全沒有價值。

options.en: Other conditions may still need to be met.
options.zh: 仍可能需要符合其他條件。

contrast.explanationZh: 不保證與沒有價值是兩回事，應看具體情境。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友覺得相關證書不是保證，就想申請時完全不提，問你怎樣看。哪句最好？

options.en: It may not be a golden ticket, but include it alongside practical examples that show what you can do.
options.zh: 它可能不是成功通行證，但應連同實際例子一起列出，展示你能做甚麼。

options.en: Remove the certificate and describe only unrelated interests because the result is not guaranteed.
options.zh: 因結果不保證，就刪證書，只描述無關興趣。

options.en: List only the certificate and leave out the practical work requested in the application.
options.zh: 只列證書，略去申請要求的實際作品。

dialogue.explanationZh: 保留資格與實際證據，既不把優勢抹去，也不把它當唯一條件。

speaking.en: A qualification can help without being a golden ticket to success.
speaking.zh: 資格可有幫助，卻不是直達成功的通行證。
speaking.promptZh: 你想同時承認優勢及其他條件。先聽，再說。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：一位有天分的新球員以為才華足以保證進校隊正選，但教練也看重持續練習及合作。用一至兩句英文說明應怎樣看待天分。

examples.en: Natural talent can help, but it is not a golden ticket to the first team. The new player still needs regular practice and good teamwork.
examples.zh: 天分有幫助，但不是直達正選隊伍的通行證。新球員仍需持續練習及良好合作。

examples.en: The player should not treat talent as a golden ticket, because earning a first-team place also involves practising consistently and working with others.
examples.zh: 球員不應把天分當成功通行證，因為爭取正選位置，也涉及持續練習及與人合作。

writing.selfCheckZh: 承認天分有幫助，但正選仍需練習及合作；不把優勢當無條件入選保證。

takeaways.en: A strong portfolio may help, but it is not a golden ticket to the place you want.
takeaways.zh: 出色作品集可能有幫助，卻不是直達理想名額的通行證。

takeaways.en: She valued the opportunity without treating it as a golden ticket.
takeaways.zh: 她珍惜機會，卻沒有把它當成功通行證。
